title: Bug
description: One confirmed bug, one file: bugs/<ID>.json in the workspace.

id.description: App prefix and a number, e.g. AL-1. Same as the file name.

area.description: Feature area, e.g. approvals, balance, permissions.

summary.description: Two or three sentences a non-programmer understands: what is wrong and who it hurts.

text.description: What should happen. For money and dates, the value worked out by hand.

basis.description: spec: a rule in the PRD says so. inferred: no PRD rule; the intent is evident from the code, the UI or common sense (say which in 'evidence').

requirement.description: Rule id from the PRD, e.g. R4 (basis spec).

link.description: Path or URL to the requirement, e.g. docs/prd.md#us-3-decide

evidence.description: For basis inferred: what shows the intended behaviour (a sibling check in the code, a label, a validation message …).

where.description: Where the cause is in the source code, if found. Leave out if not known.

file.description: Path relative to the source folder.

how.description: Confirmed two ways: what the app answered, and what is stored.

response.description: The UI or HTTP response that shows the bug.

state.description: The stored state (read-only DB query, or a fresh API read) that shows the bug.

byDesignCheck.description: Why this is not intended behaviour.

confidence.description: confirmed: reproduced and proven wrong against the spec or evident intent. likely: reproduced, but intent is not certain. question: needs a person to decide.

hint.description: A short hint for the fix: what to change.

spec.description: Workspace path of the regression spec, specs/<ID>.spec.mjs.

repro.description: Workspace path of the captioned repro script, repro/<ID>.repro.mjs.

environment.description: local, dev, staging …, plus the version tested if known.

run.description: The session (run id) that found it.
